newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude oil range-bound on ACCESS, slump seen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude oil range-bound on ACCESS, slump seen.

text.p: U.S. energy futures traded near their settlements in early after-hours ACCESS trade, with volumes fading for October ahead of Friday's crude expiry.
"People are starting to roll over positions," one ACCESS trader said.
October crude traded at about $23.45 a barrel early into ACCESS, down nine cents from the settle with 184 lots exchanged. Around 449 contracts traded in November.
Overnight, profit-taking weighed on crude with traders taking advantage of today's relatively narrow range to unload positions before further expected slumps.
Traders forecast more downside pressure on Friday with $22 and $21.70 seen as key support levels.
October heating oil and gasolines were thinly traded, with front-month unleaded up eight points from the settle at 61.40 cents a gallon and "heat" up seven points at 66.80 cents.
